stem: $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{AC}$ are two tangent segments drawn from the point $A$ to the circle $M$ whose radius is ${=r}$ cm, where $B$ and $C$ are the points of tangency. If $MA = {=d}$ cm, find the length of the chord $\overline{BC}$ in cm.
solution: $MB$ is a radius and $AB$ a tangent, so $m(\angle MBA) = 90^\circ$.
The line $MA$ passes through the centre and the intersection point of the tangents, so it is the axis of the chord $BC$: it is perpendicular to $BC$ and bisects it at $N$.
Area of triangle $MBA$: $\frac{1}{2} \times MB \times AB = \frac{1}{2} \times MA \times BN$, so $BN = \frac{{=r} \times {=t}}{{=d}} = {=r*t/d}$ cm.
notes: Radius/tangent swap gives same chord 24m. Whole-number answers: 24, 48, 72. Uses Pythagoras, area, and axis-of-chord corollary.
